purpose: The citable, digest-pinnable identity of ZKM's proof-statement and verification-key surface. The spec version string (0.1.0-draft) is identical across every ZKM revision, so family epoch zka:protocol-family:2026-08-15.1 pins the revision LABEL (0.1.0-draft (rev 10)) rather than the bare version. That label discriminates one revision from another but is still prose: it does not pin a verification key, a public-input vector, a bytecode digest or a toolchain, and nothing in the manifest forces a later breaking revision to move it. This scanner-clean public projection retains the ZKM statement surface while omitting only unavailable AFP-KDC fixture consumer claims; its statement_set_id digests the actual cryptographic surface, and scripts/check-zkm-statement-registry.py requires the family's pinned revision label to be at least last_breaking_revision, so a breaking revision the family has not followed fails ZKM's own gate.
statement_set_id_derivation: sha256 over b"zkm:statement-set:v1" || canonical-JSON(preimage), where canonical JSON is UTF-8 with object keys sorted and no insignificant whitespace (RFC 8785 subset), and preimage is exactly {"statements": [...], "retired_statements": [...], "revocation": {...}, "toolchain": {...}} built by PROJECTING each member to a fixed field list, in this order, with absent fields serialized as null: statements -> [id, circuit_package, status, current_since_revision, supersedes, value_moving, public_input_count, public_inputs, vk_hash, acir_opcode_count, bytecode_sha256]; retired_statements -> [id, retired_in_revision, superseded_by, public_input_count, post_cutover_registry, reinterpretation]; revocation -> [scheme, construction, depth, accepted_scheme_values, superseded_scheme]; toolchain -> the whole object. Array order is preserved as published. Prose fields (note, reason, notes) are DELIBERATELY excluded: an editorial edit is not a protocol change, and an id that moved on prose would train reviewers to re-bless it. Recomputed on every CI run by scripts/check-zkm-statement-registry.py.

statements.note: Carries no ZKA value leg (no note root, no ZKA nullifier, no output commitments, no asset_id): that absence is what makes this key structurally incapable of authorizing value movement.
The only value-moving ZKM statement. A settlement target's value-moving entry point MUST accept this key and no other.
Delegation possession companion, matched at settlement on cm_out_1 / nf / settlement context.
Well-formed depth-0 insertion; every accepted leaf provably has a living revocation authority.
The ONLY key a target may accept to authorize a revocation insertion. Its public vector IS the insertion authorization.

Continuity companion only: empty-leaf previous_root and full-id next_root use the same canonical path and siblings. Requires separately verified revocation-auth:v1 with matching root_id and context; the target binds the current tip and epoch and commits insertion plus publication atomically.
Publishes NO root_id, so it cannot be replayed as a revocation authorization. A registry that maps this statement to the revocation-auth key destroys that property.
Credential-bound issuance: same KDC entity seed derives the principal issuance key and the ZKC handle.

Non-settling companion. Acceptable only alongside a zkm:spend-conjoined:v2 proof matched atomically on nf, zka_cm_recipient, asset_id and settlement context. Rev 13 corrects the KDC seed -> spending key -> viewing key -> address chain. The v1 identifier and five public inputs retain their intended same-subject meaning; the rev-13 statement_set_id and corrected VK are mandatory compatibility pins, and pre-rev-13 VKs MUST be removed atomically. Retaining the identifier avoids an unrelated effect-profile allowlist/digest change.

retired_statements.reason: revocation_scheme added to the public vector; depth-128 low-half exclusion slot replaced by the depth-254 full-identifier tree; verification key re-blessed.
revocation_scheme added to the public vector; depth-128 low-half exclusion slot replaced by the depth-254 full-identifier tree; verification key re-blessed.

revision_history.summary: v1 transition statements retired; revocation_scheme = 2 added to both transition vectors (13 -> 14 and 8 -> 9 elements); depth-128 low-half revocation slot replaced by the depth-254 full-identifier exclusion tree; every verification key re-blessed.

This registry and the v1-to-v2 cutover note published. No statement, ABI, verification key or revocation scheme moved: the statement_set_id is unchanged from rev 10, which is exactly what a non-breaking revision is required to look like.

Noir beta.22 -> beta.25 and Barretenberg 5.0.0-nightly.20260522 -> 5.0.0; all eight verification keys re-blessed. The mandate-transition and spend-conjoined ACIR/bytecode identities also moved; statement identifiers, public-input vectors, and revocation semantics are unchanged.

Adds verified revocation insertion continuity and atomic ordered publication; corrects recipient derivation through the KDC spending key; requires positive private spends while retaining both outputs; corrects mandate-only policy-witness diagnostics. Public vectors, identifier lifecycle, revocation scheme and proving toolchain remain unchanged. The spend and recipient verification keys move; the mandate-only verification key is unchanged despite its diagnostic bytecode change. Consumers must atomically repin the combined statement set and remove earlier keys. The independent effect-profile identity is preserved.

version_discipline.breaking_change: Adding, retiring or renaming a statement identifier; changing any public-input vector (order, name, type or count); moving any verification key, ACIR opcode count or bytecode digest; changing the accepted revocation scheme; or moving the pinned toolchain.
rules: A breaking change MUST append a revision_history entry whose statement_set_id differs from its predecessor's and whose breaking flag is true.
last_breaking_revision MUST equal the greatest revision whose revision_history entry is breaking.
A non-breaking revision MUST carry the predecessor's statement_set_id unchanged.

The family manifest MUST discriminate ZKM by at least one of a revision label in protocols.zkm.version or a sha256 pin of this file; a bare version string is not discrimination, and ZKM's gate fails closed on it even when this registry agrees with it.

A breaking revision MUST be followed by the family manifest: a pinned revision label MUST be at least last_breaking_revision, and MUST NOT name a revision ZKM has not published. ZKM's own gate fails closed while it is not, so a breaking ZKM revision cannot be silently combined with an epoch pinned to an older statement surface.

The family interface manifest SHOULD additionally pin this file by sha256 (artifact binding or projection assertion). The revision label discriminates revisions but is prose: it does not move when a verification key, public-input vector, bytecode digest or toolchain pin moves within a revision.

A consumer holding only a family epoch pin and a bare 0.1.0-draft version string, with no revision label and no digest, MUST treat ZKM's statement surface as unpinned and MUST NOT accept ZKM proofs on that basis.

revision_label.note: Epoch 2026-10-26.1 advances the revision label and statement-set identity together for the combined breaking rev 13. The published canonical snapshot names observed ZKA target merge b0f255e2340e8b0092422e50a3abac12cb452cec and closes the component-staging window; deployment adoption remains a separate reviewed atomic cutover.

statement_digest.reason: Pinned by the canonical family manifest's projections.zkm assertion zkm-statement-set-id, a json_pointer_equals on /statement_set_id of this file, enforced on every ZKM run by the shared family validator. This public snapshot supplies a scanner-clean projection of that manifest and lock, not a canonical-family mirror. scripts/check-zkm-statement-registry.py accepts three pin forms: an artifact_bindings entry for this path (whole-file sha256), a projections.zkm sha256_equals assertion on this path (whole-file sha256), or a projections.zkm json_pointer_equals assertion on /statement_set_id (field pin). The field pin is preferred over a whole-file digest: statement_set_id commits to every statement, ABI, verification-key, revocation and toolchain field but deliberately excludes prose (note/reason fields), so an editorial edit cannot break the family pin, whereas a whole-file digest moves on prose and would force a new family epoch plus consumer snapshot resyncs for every editorial change.

consumer_gate.description: The checks a downstream consumer's own CI SHOULD execute against a ZKM checkout before accepting ZKM proofs at a settlement target.
